gaps.sentence: They worked ___ a compromise after hours of discussion.
gaps.explanation: work out = find the solution to; understand; also exercise.

gaps.sentence: This old house needs doing ___ before winter.
gaps.explanation: do up = repair and decorate a building. (British usage)

gaps.sentence: Please fill ___ this form and sign at the bottom.
gaps.explanation: fill in/out a form (British prefers in).
run out OF something = have none left.

gaps.sentence: He ended ___ selling insurance, though he'd trained as a chef.
gaps.explanation: end up = finally be in a place/situation/state.

gaps.sentence: They want to try ___ the new software before buying.
gaps.explanation: try out = test something to see if it works.

gaps.sentence: She always gets round ___ washing up by promising to do it later.
gaps.explanation: get round to = finally find time for; here: avoid a duty — test the preposition after get round.
